vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: correlation-memory
Version: 2.0.3

The correlation-memory plugin is a well-documented and focused tool for enhancing memory searches within the OpenClaw environment. The core logic in `index.ts` is restricted to read-only filesystem operations, specifically loading correlation rules from a local JSON file, and contains no network requests, credential access, or environment variable harvesting. The uninstaller script (`uninstall.sh`) follows safe practices, including configuration backups and verification steps, and the overall package lacks any indicators of malicious intent, obfuscation, or prompt-injection attacks.

llm.summary: The plugin's code and instructions mostly match its stated purpose (correlating memory searches), but the SKILL.md makes contradictory claims about network/write behavior and the bundle includes an uninstall script that edits config — review install/uninstall steps and your correlation rules (which can surface sensitive memory) before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (correlation-aware memory search) align with the provided code: index.ts implements rule loading, matching, and tool registration and reads rules from memory/correlation-rules.json. However the SKILL.md repeatedly claims "zero external dependencies" and "no writes," while installation steps require git clone and npm install (network) and the repo contains an uninstall.sh that performs backups and edits openclaw.json (writes). This is a minor but important inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs cloning from GitHub and running npm install (network+disk write) and to add the plugin to openclaw.json. Runtime instructions in index.ts keep to reading rules and doing local read-only operations, but the repository includes an uninstall script that will back up and modify OpenClaw config and the docs recommend placing/using scripts (heartbeat/surfacing) which may run regularly. Also the example correlation rules include sensitive-sounding contexts (e.g., "access-log", "credential") — the plugin will fetch whatever contexts are present in workspace memory, so rule content and memory files can cause exposure.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automated install spec in the registry; SKILL.md instructs git clone from a GitHub repo and npm install. GitHub and npm are standard hosts (lower risk than arbitrary URLs), and package-lock.json is included so you can inspect exact dependencies. This requires network access and will write files to ~/.openclaw/extensions — not truly "no external deps" at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared requirements list no environment variables or credentials. index.ts does not read env vars. The uninstall script accepts an optional OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH env var (to override config path) but that is optional. Overall requested environment/credentials are proportional to the plugin's stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The plugin does not set always:true and follows normal OpenClaw plugin invocation patterns. It registers tools that can be invoked or used automatically by the agent. The uninstall script, however, writes to and restores OpenClaw config during uninstall — this is expected for the uninstall task but represents config-modifying behavior in the bundle and should be reviewed before running.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing:

- Understand the real install actions: the SKILL.md asks you to git clone from GitHub and run npm install. That fetches code and writes to ~/.openclaw/extensions — the "zero external dependencies" claim applies to runtime but not install. Inspect the repo and package-lock.json before running npm install.
- Inspect the uninstall.sh and any scripts in the repo before executing: uninstall.sh will back up and modify your openclaw.json (writes to config). Only run it if you trust the repo and after making your own backups.
- Audit correlation rules and your workspace memory: rules can reference contexts like "access-log", "credential", or other sensitive names; when a rule matches the plugin will fetch those contexts from your workspace memory. Review memory/correlation-rules.json (and any memory files) to ensure sensitive data won't be surfaced.
- Run in an isolated/staging environment first: verify behavior, run tests (npm test), and monitor gateway logs after installing. Confirm OpenClaw version compatibility (>= 2026.1.26) and Node version requirements.
- Verify the GitHub source and maintainer: the registry metadata lists an owner ID but no homepage; prefer installing from an official or well-known repo and check commit history/signatures where possible.
- If you need stronger assurances: vendor the code (download/verify source offline), inspect index.ts and package-lock.json for unexpected dependencies or scripts, then install locally rather than executing install scripts blindly.

If you want, I can:
- Summarize package.json/package-lock.json entries and highlight any non-obvious dependencies or postinstall scripts,
- Extract and summarize uninstall.sh contents so you can review exactly what it modifies,
- Scan index.ts for any hidden network access or environment accesses beyond what's already visible.
